subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw support `openclaw.yaml`/`openclaw.yml` as first-class config files, or keep the canonical JSON5 `openclaw.json` contract and improve the supported editing tools/docs instead?
rationale: This is not a broken existing behavior report; it expands the core config-file contract and requires a maintainer call on compatibility, security, parser semantics, and long-term support cost.

options.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Keep `openclaw.json` as the only canonical runtime config file and improve docs/tooling around `openclaw config set/get`, Control UI config editing, and `config.patch` for comment-preserving edits.

options.title: Design YAML Support
options.body: Accept YAML only after a design covers file precedence, write-back format, includes, validation, doctor behavior, security review, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Defer Until Tooling Gap Is Proven
options.body: Leave this open as a low-priority ergonomics request until config.patch/CLI editing still proves insufficient for real users.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Keep `openclaw.json` as the only canonical runtime config file and improve docs/tooling around `openclaw config set/get`, Control UI config editing, and `config.patch` for comment-preserving edits.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal for the config IO and compatibility policy surface points to Peter Steinberger.
